lines:
Direction: the LLM summary is the single worst-value token in a run. Evidence gathered 2026-09-26.

THE MEASUREMENT. On a decode-bound local model the summary decodes at the worst possible moment - the whole span prefilled, context at its longest, and a single sequence with no batching. Measured: the local qwen here produced a 5,959-token summary in 481 s (12.4 tok/s) while the same run averaged 21.2 tok/s (chat.3fdeab43, 213,609 output in 168 min). The operator's qwen3-27b on a 5090 compacted twice in a ~100-minute run, ~11 min each; that run has produced 296,555 output tokens at 49.4 tok/s average, so ~22k summary tokens (7% of the output) cost ~22 min (22% of the wall clock). On a fast cloud model the same work is trivial: the measured 100k deepseek run summarised 53,348 shadowed tokens into 4,518 output tokens in 16.6 s for $0.006 (cap 6,606; prompt 69,411 tokens of which 68,992 cached; the call produced no reasoning at all). So this is primarily a decode-bound-model problem and a complexity reduction everywhere: at a 1M window the same share plans a 95,402-token summary, which is 1.5 hours of local decode and $0.11-0.24 of cloud tokens for one compaction.

WHAT ALREADY NEEDS NO LLM. The durable state block (live goal, Run task list, touched files) is re-derived from records; task 139's own reasoning is that "the objective, the plan and prior reads must not depend on the summariser keeping them". User turns are pinned verbatim (task 137). The retained tail is verbatim by construction. Tool results are pruned head+tail without a model. Originals stay durably retrievable and the model can re-read them. What is missing is only an *index* of the span that was dropped.

WHAT THE LEDGER CAN BE BUILT FROM (no provider call). The dropped units are `ModelToolExchangeV1`s: `assistant_content` carries each ToolCall's name and arguments plus the assistant's Text and Reasoning, and `results` carries each outcome with is_error and content. So a checkpoint can be written entirely by code, bounded by the same budget B (so post-compaction occupancy is unchanged, `R + S = B`).

PROPOSED SHAPE. Per dropped exchange, one line naming the tool and its target and outcome: `read src/engine.js -> 16,698 bytes`, `edit src/main.js -> old 412/new 655 chars`, `shell node selfcheck.js -> exit 0`, `job.output -> 1,204 bytes`. Repeated operations collapse: a path read or a command run N times becomes one line with N and the last outcome (the measured run re-read the same files and re-ran selfcheck many times). One intent line per dropped assistant turn, extracted from that turn's own visible text, falling back to the head of its reasoning. A failures-and-fixes section for non-zero outcomes, each with the first line of the assistant text that followed it. Then the existing state block, pinned user turns, retained tail, and a marker saying the originals remain retrievable. Rough size: the 100k run shadowed 16 units / 53,348 tokens, so a ledger for that span is on the order of 1,000 tokens - against the 4,518 tokens the model wrote, and with zero decode and zero latency.

WHAT IT ALSO REMOVES. With no auxiliary call there is no output cap to choose, no summary failure class, no shrink/retry ladder, no auxiliary provider or model setting for that mode, no framed-summary shrink check, and no prefix-cache concern for the summary request. Task 144's drop path is already a degenerate version of this: it keeps the newest units that fit, a marker and the state block. This task generalises it from a failure fallback into a first-class strategy.

RESEARCH CONFIRMATION, 2026-09-26 (web search). (1) "The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management", arXiv:2508.21433 (DL4C @ NeurIPS 2025, JetBrains Research): a controlled comparison in SWE-agent on SWE-bench Verified across five model configurations, plus an OpenHands generality probe. Both strategies more than halve cost against the raw agent; observation masking matches and sometimes slightly exceeds LLM summarization's solve rate. With Qwen3-Coder-480B, masking is 52% cheaper than the raw agent AND 2.6% higher solve rate, and $0.03/instance cheaper than summarization ($15 over 500 instances). Their hybrid, masking plus a summary, is a further 7% cheaper than masking alone and 11% cheaper than summarization. Their masking keeps the full reasoning and action chain and replaces only environment observations older than a window; they also report a trajectory-elongation effect, where summarization lengthens trajectories - the same shape as the operator's 296k-output run. (2) Anthropic ships the non-LLM form in production as context editing: `clear_tool_uses_20250919` clears the oldest tool results in chronological order and replaces each with placeholder text (optionally also clearing tool inputs), and `clear_thinking_20251015` clears thinking blocks under a `keep` policy. Both are applied without any model call. (3) AGORA, arXiv:2605.26596, warns against the obvious shortcut: token-level extractive compression collapses on agents - every one of 17 (env, backbone, method) cells fell to mean reward <= 0.05 despite 1.3-13.3x compression - because the tokens carrying action semantics are exactly the lowest self-information ones ("action-grammar destruction"). Their fix is step granularity with an always-keep floor for format- and recency-critical content; their ablation finds the structural floor, not the learned 125M scorer, is the dominant quality lever.

REFINEMENTS FROM THAT READING. (a) Compress observations, not the narrative: when folding a span, keep each dropped turn's own visible text and a bounded head of its reasoning, and mask or index its observations. The measured design above drops whole exchanges including the assistant's text; the paper's masking keeps the reasoning/action chain and condenses observations, so the ledger should bias the same way. (b) Build the ledger from durable records (the ToolRecordStore outcomes already used for touched files) rather than only from the dropped bytes, so a checkpoint is a projection of records and never a summary of a previous summary; recursion is where drift comes from, and the dropped span contains the previous checkpoint. Fall back to the dropped units where a record does not exist. (c) Order the layers mask -> ledger -> optional small capped summary, because the hybrid is the best-performing variant measured and that ordering is also what a low summaryShare now expresses. Also confirmed by (3): never compress inside an action. We already only prune tool results (never tool calls) and only drop whole units, which is precisely the failure mode AGORA measured.

OPEN DECISIONS. (a) Default mode: keep the model-written summary and add the extractive one as a per-model Settings choice, or make extractive the default and the model summary the opt-in. (b) Whether the ledger keeps a truncated reasoning head per dropped turn (better "why", a few hundred tokens) or only the assistant's visible text. (c) The ledger budget: my default is the same S the share computes, though the ledger rarely needs a tenth of it.

ACCEPTANCE. On the same benchmark with a local model, no compaction stall longer than a few seconds and a wall clock reduced by the compaction share; on the 100k deepseek benchmark, conformance stays (53/53 self-check, the same 8 files) with no regression in uncached tokens or cost; `context.compacted` records `strategy: "extractive"` with the ledger's section sizes and the units it folded; and the existing guarantees stay green - strict shrink, balanced boundaries, exactly-once lifecycle, durable replay, instruction restoration, and generated state never pinned as user direction. The A/B is cheap: two runs at 100k on deepseek cost about $0.25 each and the model-written summary is already measured for comparison.

BOUNDARIES. Owns how a checkpoint is written when no summariser is used, and the fallback ladder when a model-written summary is chosen but fails. Does not own the compaction budgets (share model, tasks 143/144), which units may be shadowed (task 137), the state block's content (task 139), or the retrieval path for originals. Related: task 148 (append-only state emission) already removes the mid-context rewrite cost and is complementary.

data.title: A checkpoint written by code instead of a decoded summary: index, extract, no model call
